result.title: MCD: Causal Distillation of Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) exhibit strong multimodal in-context learning (ICL) capabilities, yet this ability degrades substantially as model size decreases. Knowledge distillation offers a natural way to bridge this gap, but existing methods primarily align output distributions or hidden representations directly. Such alignment teaches the student what the teacher predicts without revealing which evidence in the complex context causally supports that prediction. Consequently, a student can imitate the teacher's answer while continuing to rely on language priors, prompt structure, or other spurious cues. To address this limitation, we introduce Multimodal Causal Distillation (MCD), a distillation framework that transfers how a strong teacher uses multimodal evidence during ICL. MCD uses structure-preserving token interventions to identify and verify causal evidence, then transfers how the teacher responds when that evidence is retained or removed. This design connects distillation to the causal patterns by which the model uses contextual evidence during multimodal ICL. Experiments across three LVLM families and seven benchmarks show that MCD improves student performance by 7.23 points on average and outperforms vanilla distillation by 4.68 points, while further analyses confirm the generalizability of these gains.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出多模态因果蒸馏（MCD）：通过保持结构的 token 干预识别并验证教师模型在 ICL 中真正依赖的因果证据，再让学生学习教师在证据保留/移除时的响应方式，从而在三个 LVLM 家族、七个基准上提升小模型性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 涉及 VLM 推理中「答案是否真正使用视觉证据」与视觉旁路、虚假线索问题，其因果干预识别证据的思路可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被用于答案、以及贡献分配与监督信号设计。
